messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug report describes an unexpected EOF (End Of File) exception when reading a CPIO archive, including archives created by the tested library or OSX command line tool. 

The failing test code writes two entries to a CPIO archive and then reads them back using CpioArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry(), which internally calls getNextCPIOEntry(). 

Inside getNextCPIOEntry(), the code first reads 2 bytes to identify the magic number of the archive entry format. It then decides which specific reading method to call based on the magic number. This could be one of the old binary format (with or without swapped half words), new format, CRC format or ASCII format. 

The readFully() method used to read bytes throws an EOFException if it tries to read beyond the end of the input stream (count < 0). This explains the EOFException described in the bug report.

The problem likely arises if the CPIO archive used for unpacking is truncated or malformed, or uses an encoding of an entry header that is not recognized. In such cases, reading bytes to identify and parse the header leads to unexpected EOF.

The unpacking code does not appear to have any intermediate validation or fallback mechanisms when reading the header bytes or entries. It directly trusts that the bytes are available and correctly formatted according to one of the expected magic numbers.

Hence, the root cause is that the getNextCPIOEntry() method and underlying readFully() call do not robustly handle truncated or altered CPIO archives and throw EOFException when the bytes cannot be read as expected.

This diagnosis matches the bug report describing EOFException on unpacking CPIO archives created through various tools. The code snippet of the test also confirms the use of getNextEntry() which delegates to getNextCPIOEntry() to read the headers triggering the EOFException on corrupted or unexpected input.

Next, I can check if there are any comments or usages about error handling in getNextCPIOEntry or related methods to verify or understand what the intended error handling approach is.

"
     * Reads the next CPIO file entry and positions stream at the beginning of
     * the entry data.
     * 
     * @return the CPIOArchiveEntry just read
     * @throws IOException
     *             if an I/O error has occurred or if a CPIO file error has
     *             occurred
     "

Diagnosis (enhanced):
- The getNextCPIOEntry method reads the next CPIO entry header from the input stream based on magic numbers identifying the format.
- It relies on readFully to read the required bytes for the header. readFully throws EOFException if the input stream ends prematurely.
- The javadoc of getNextCPIOEntry explicitly mentions throwing IOException on errors, including CPIO file errors.
- The reported EOFException is consistent with readFully encountering premature end of stream when input archive is truncated or malformed.
- The test reproducing this problem reads entries from archives that may have unexpected or unsupported magic numbers or truncated data, leading to EOFException during header reads.
- There is no special error handling or recovery to avoid EOFException in getNextCPIOEntry or readFully.
- This aligns with the bug report that archives created by external tools (like OSX cpio) or the library itself cause EOFException on CPIO unpacking.
- The root cause is that the CpioArchiveInputStream does not robustly handle truncated or corrupted archives and simply throws EOFException when the expected header bytes cannot be read fully.

This diagnosis covers the bug report symptoms, test behavior, and source code implementation details. The EOFException comes from the low-level reads of archive entry headers, triggered by truncated/altered archive inputs.

Next, I can check code snippets from readOldBinaryEntry and readOldAsciiEntry, etc, that parse headers after detecting the magic to further confirm no additional robustness or special handling is applied after initial readFully calls.
